bugs.creator: gridge
bugs.summary: scan() crashes interactive R when opening an unz() connection for a missing member

comments.text:
Description
===========

In a clean interactive R 4.6.1 session on Windows, passing a closed unz() connection to scan() causes R to terminate if the requested ZIP member does not exist.

The expected warning and error are printed, but R then exits instead of returning to the prompt.

This reproduces with R.exe --vanilla and Rgui.exe. It does not require any contributed packages or an external ZIP file.

Minimal reproducible example
============================

Start an interactive session with:

    R.exe --vanilla

Then run:

    z <- tempfile(fileext = ".zip")

    # Write a valid empty ZIP archive with a one-byte prefix.
    writeBin(
        as.raw(c(0, 0x50, 0x4b, 0x05, 0x06, rep(0, 18))),
        z
    )

    unzip(z, list = TRUE)  # successfully reports an empty archive

    con <- unz(z, "missing.txt")
    scan(con, nlines = 1, what = "", sep = "\n")

Observed result
===============

R prints:

    Error in scan(con, nlines = 1, what = "", sep = "\n") :
      cannot open the connection
    In addition: Warning message:
    In scan(con, nlines = 1, what = "", sep = "\n") :
      cannot locate file 'missing.txt' in zip file '...'

The interactive R process then terminates.

Windows Error Reporting records an access violation in R.dll:

    Exception code: 0xc0000005

Two observed R.dll exception offsets were:

    0x00000000000b16c9
    0x00000000000b16d5

Expected result
===============

scan() should issue the warning and error and return control to the interactive R prompt. A missing ZIP member should not terminate R.

Source analysis
===============

do_scan() in src/main/scan.c installs scan_cleanup() as a context cleanup handler before attempting to open the connection.

When the connection is initially closed:

    data.wasopen = data.con->isopen;
    if (!data.wasopen) {
        ...
        if (!data.con->open(data.con))
            error(_("cannot open the connection"));
    }

When unz_open() returns FALSE because the member is absent, error() unwinds the context. scan_cleanup() then executes:

    if (ld->con && !ld->ttyflag && !ld->wasopen) {
        ld->con->close(ld->con);
        ld->con = NULL;
    }

This calls close() because the connection was not previously open. It does not check whether the attempted open succeeded or whether the connection is currently open.

R_newunz() allocates its private structure with malloc():

    new->private = (void *) malloc(sizeof(struct unzconn));

The uf field is not initialized. When unz_open() fails, no valid handle is stored in private->uf. The erroneous cleanup call reaches unz_close(), which retrieves and dereferences that uninitialized handle.

Disassembly of the installed R.dll maps the observed exception offsets inside the inlined unz_close()/unzCloseCurrentFile() path.

The same scan_cleanup() condition is present in current R-devel source as checked on 2026-08-19.

Possible fix
============

scan_cleanup() should only invoke close() when the attempted open succeeded:

    if (ld->con && !ld->ttyflag && !ld->wasopen) {
        if (ld->con->isopen)
            ld->con->close(ld->con);
        ld->con = NULL;
    }

As an additional defensive measure, R_newunz() could initialize private->uf to NULL, and unz_close() could tolerate a NULL handle.

The R 4.6.0 change that added filename termination and validation in unzLocateFile() does not address this failed-open cleanup path.

Session information
===================

R version 4.6.1 (2026-06-24 ucrt)
Platform: x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64
Running under: Windows 11 x64 (build 26200)

Matrix products: default
LAPACK version 3.12.1

attached base packages:
[1] stats graphics grDevices utils datasets methods base

loaded via a namespace:
[1] compiler_4.6.1
